exposure: Uterine malformations (unicornuate, complete bicornuate, didelphic uterus) resulting in hemi-uterus pregnancy
cohort: 336 women who gave birth at a single hospital between 2015 and 2021, including 112 with hemi-uterus pregnancies and 224 with normal uteruses
finding: Women with hemi-uterus pregnancies due to uterine malformations were at significantly higher risk for several adverse pregnancy outcomes, including preterm birth, preterm premature rupture of membranes, malpresentation, and cesarean section, compared to women with normal uteruses.
mod_finding: Cesarean section rates were significantly higher in the hemi-uterus pregnancy group compared to the normal uterus group.
